items.title: Michelle Zauner (Japanese Breakfast) Announces New Memoir Thank You For Your Suffering
items.summary:
Michelle Zauner, the musician who records as Japanese Breakfast, has set a second memoir for release. Thank You For Your Suffering arrives April 27th, 2027, following Crying in H Mart, her 2021 account of her mother's death that became a New York Times bestseller.

The new book picks up years after that loss. Zauner finds a diary her mother kept in Korean and, unable to read it, sets out to learn the language — a project that eventually takes her to Seoul for a year with her husband and bandmate, Peter Bradley.

According to Consequence, the memoir covers her time in an intensive language program, the adjustment to living in the city, and the strain the move placed on her marriage. It also tracks the lighter parts of the year: new friendships, the city's underground scene, time with her maternal aunt, and her early attempts at writing songs in Korean.

Zauner has been signaling the project for a while. She told The Korea Times in 2024 that she was enrolled at Sogang University's Korean Language Education Center and intended to write about it, and told Harper's Bazaar the following year that she wanted the language in order to talk with her aunt about her mother — conversations that deepened as her Korean improved.

Japanese Breakfast released its most recent album, For Melancholy Brunettes (& sad women), in March 2025. Pre-orders for Thank You For Your Suffering are open now.

items.title: Edie Falco To Star In Legal Drama ‘Katie Greaves’ Ordered To Series By Fox
items.summary:
Fox has ordered the legal drama Katie Greaves to series, with Edie Falco starring in the title role. The show, currently carrying a working title, comes from writer Sharr White, Scott Free Productions and Fox Entertainment Studios, and is set to premiere during the 2027-28 season.

White, a playwright whose television credits include Apple TV's Presumed Innocent and Palm Royale, wrote the series and will serve as showrunner. Falco plays a New Hampshire public defender who left the job after a personal tragedy and is now raising her two young granddaughters with her husband when the work pulls her back in.

Deadline reported that the pickup was one of three Fox drama contenders identified in January, alongside The Interrogator — greenlit in February for 2026-27 — and Tom Szentgyorgyi's Blood Ties. Word of the Katie Greaves order circulated for roughly two weeks before the network finalized it by casting Falco, part of a pattern at Fox that also produced Best Medicine with Josh Charles and Memory of a Killer with Patrick Dempsey in final talks.

"Sharr has created an extraordinary character in Katie Greaves: funny, formidable, deeply human, and driven to fight for people who might otherwise be overlooked, including her own family," said Michael Thorn, President of the Fox Television Network, adding that Falco "brings all of that strength, wit, and vulnerability to the screen."

Falco, White, and Scott Free's Ridley Scott and David W. Zucker executive produce, with Fox Entertainment Studios producing and Fox Entertainment Global handling worldwide distribution. That ownership structure is the point: Katie Greaves is the second 2027-28 series Fox has ordered from its own studio, after the comedy Mammoth.

Falco won three Emmys as Carmela Soprano on The Sopranos and a fourth for Nurse Jackie. She recently wrapped the fifth and final season of Paramount+'s Mayor of Kingstown opposite Jeremy Renner, and appears in Avatar: Fire and Ash.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Announces Soundtrack Album with Tracks from Travis Scott, Morgan Wallen and Keith Richards
items.summary:
Rockstar Games has announced Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, a 34-track companion record of original music built for the game. The album arrives November 19th, the same day Grand Theft Auto VI launches.

Six songs went up on streaming services immediately, and the lineup is unusually wide. Travis Scott's "RHYNO" is produced by Daft Punk's Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo; Morgan Wallen contributes "Last Thing You Need"; and Keith Richards of the Rolling Stones appears on "Bright Lights, Big City."

The rest of the opening batch runs from Rauw Alejandro's "Macacoa 2000" to Yung Lean's "That's It," featuring Future and Metro Boomin, plus "Sexy Magic," a collaboration between CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, PinkPantheress, Fred again.. and Etienne de Crécy. As Consequence noted, the remaining 28 tracks will be revealed later.

Pre-orders for the album opened September 17th in several vinyl and CD configurations. The game itself is available to pre-order on Xbox and PlayStation 5, with pre-loads starting November 12th ahead of the November 19th release.

items.title: Soccer Mommy Returns With New Song “Rings of Saturn”
items.summary:
Soccer Mommy has released "Rings of Saturn," the first new song from Sophie Allison in two years. Elliott Kozel, who has worked with Rosalía and Björk, produced the track, and Suji Park directed the accompanying video.

Allison described the song as coming out of a low period. "This song is about feeling lost and looking for hope from anywhere," she said. "I wrote it during a difficult time when I would often take my telescope out into the yard to look at the moon or at planets. There's something about feeling small that can kind of take the weight off."

Her most recent album, Evergreen, arrived in 2024, followed by a stripped-down acoustic version of the record. Pitchfork noted that Allison opened two dates on Liz Phair and Sleater-Kinney's Flannel and the Fury Tour last week.

Next up is a co-headlining run with Snail Mail, which begins September 30 in Charlotte.

items.title: ‘Miami Vice ’85’: John Leguizamo to Play the Bad Guy in Joseph Kosinski’s Crime Thriller (Exclusive)
items.summary:
John Leguizamo has joined Miami Vice '85, Joseph Kosinski's feature adaptation of the 1980s crime series for Universal. He will play the film's main villain, according to The Hollywood Reporter.

Leguizamo joins a cast that already includes Michael B. Jordan as Ricardo Tubbs and Austin Butler as James Crockett, alongside Alden Ehrenreich, Whitney Peak, Camila Morrone and Danny Ramirez. Kosinski, who directed Top Gun: Maverick and F1, is shooting the film for Imax with production eyed for a November start in New York and Miami.

The project draws on the pilot of the Anthony Yerkovich-created series that starred Don Johnson and Philip Michael Thomas as undercover Miami detectives, and is pitched around the glamour and corruption of the mid-1980s city. Universal has dated it for May 19, 2028. Dylan Clark produces through Dylan Clark Productions alongside Kosinski.

The casting extends a busy stretch for Leguizamo at the studio. He played Eumaeus opposite Matt Damon in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, which has grossed $1.68 billion to become Universal's highest-earning film ever, and he reunites with Damon on an untitled project from the Daniels now shooting in Los Angeles.

He also appears in The Exorcist: Martyrs, Mike Flanagan's reboot that Universal opens March 12, 2027. Leguizamo recently published a Scholastic children's book, Kiki and the Can, with artwork by the graffiti artist John "Crash" Matos.
